Hybrid Framework for Robotic Manipulation:
Integrating Reinforcement Learning and Large
Language Models
Md Saad
Department of Mechanical Engineering,
Jamia Millia Islamia,
New Delhi, India
mohammed.saadsalik@gmail.comSajjad Hussain
School of Architecture,
Technology and Engineering,
University of Brighton,
Brighton, UK
s.hussain4@brighton.ac.ukMohd Suhaib
Department of Mechanical Engineering,
Jamia Millia Islamia
New Delhi, India
msuhaib@jmi.ac.in
Abstract—This paper introduces a new hybrid framework that
combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large Language
Models (LLMs) to improve robotic manipulation tasks. By
utilizing RL for accurate low-level control and LLMs for high-
level task planning and understanding of natural language,
the proposed framework effectively connects low-level execution
with high-level reasoning in robotic systems. This integration
allows robots to understand and carry out complex, human-like
instructions while adapting to changing environments in real-
time. The framework is tested in a PyBullet-based simulation
environment using the Franka Emika Panda robotic arm, with
various manipulation scenarios as benchmarks. The results show
a 33.5% decrease in task completion time and enhancements
of 18.1% and 36.4% in accuracy and adaptability, respectively,
when compared to systems that use only RL. These results
underscore the potential of LLM-enhanced robotic systems for
practical applications, making them more efficient, adaptable,
and capable of interacting with humans. Future research will
aim to explore sim-to-real transfer, scalability, and multi-robot
systems to further broaden the framework’s applicability.
Keywords:Robotic Manipulation, Reinforcement Learning
Large Language Models (LLMs), Task Execution.
I. INTRODUCTION
In recent years, the field of robotics has seen significant
growth, largely due to advancements in artificial intelligence
(AI) and machine learning (ML) [1]. One of the standout de-
velopments in this area is Reinforcement Learning (RL), which
has proven highly effective in enabling robots to carry out
low-level control tasks like manipulation and navigation with
impressive precision and autonomy [2]. Concurrently, Large
Language Models (LLMs) have transformed natural language
understanding and task planning, providing capabilities for
reasoning and decision-making that resemble human thought
processes [3]. However, even with the progress made in these
separate areas, the opportunity to merge RL and LLMs to
develop more intelligent and adaptable robotic systems has
not been fully explored [4].This paper aims to fill that gap by introducing a hybrid
framework that combines RL for executing low-level tasks
with LLMs for high-level task planning and decision-making.
This integration allows robots to comprehend and carry out
complex, human-like instructions while adjusting to changing
environments. By harnessing the advantages of both RL and
LLMs, the proposed framework seeks to improve efficiency,
accuracy, and adaptability in robotic manipulation tasks. The
framework is evaluated in a PyBullet-based simulation envi-
ronment using the Franka Emika Panda robotic arm, where
various manipulation scenarios serve as benchmarks for as-
sessing its performance.
II. RELATEDWORK
The integration of Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large
Language Models (LLMs) in robotics has become a hot
topic in recent years. Gomes et al [5] investigated deep
RL for robotic pick-and-place tasks, achieving an impressive
84% accuracy by utilizing MobileNet and depth cameras for
robotic grasping in simulated environments. Shahid et al [6]
showcased the effectiveness of continuous control actions for
robotic manipulation through the Proximal Policy Optimiza-
tion (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithms. Their
research achieved a remarkable 100 % success rate in grasp-
ing tasks with the Franka Emika Panda robot, successfully
transferring learned behaviors from simulations to real-world
scenarios.
Chu et al [7] introduced Lafite-RL, a framework that utilizes
LLM feedback to speed up RL training. Their findings showed
notable improvements in learning rates compared to traditional
RL approaches. Likewise, Liu et al [8] proposed a self-
corrected multimodal LLM framework for end-to-end robot
manipulation, achieving 79 % accuracy on known objects
and 69 % on unseen categories by incorporating an error
rectification mechanism. In the realm of agricultural robotics,
Che et al [9] highlighted the potential of merging generative AIarXiv:2603.30022v1  [cs.RO]  31 Mar 2026

and computer vision for intelligent robotic systems, surpassing
conventional methods in agricultural picking tasks despite
facing environmental challenges. Other researchers have also
explored the wider applications of LLMs in robotics. Wang
et al [3] provided a thorough review of LLMs in robotics,
emphasizing the opportunities and challenges that come with
their integration into robotic systems. Kwon et al [10] demon-
strated the practicality of using LLMs as zero-shot trajectory
generators, illustrating that LLMs can create low-level trajec-
tories for robotic manipulation using straightforward prompts.
Mower et al [11] introduced ROS-LLM, a framework that links
LLMs with the Robot Operating System (ROS), making robot
programming more accessible for non-experts through natural
language.
Recent advances in robotics emphasize combining high-
level semantic reasoning with low-level control for improved
adaptability. Reinforcement Learning (RL) has shown success
in control tasks but struggles with interpreting complex in-
structions. This gap is addressed by integrating Large Lan-
guage Models (LLMs), which enable robots to understand
and generalize tasks through language [12]. Jain et al. [13]
introduced dynamic reward specification via natural language.
Huang et al. [14] proposed InnerMonologue for internal task
reasoning. Ahn et al. [15] developed SayCan, grounding LLM
plans through feasibility scoring. Jiang et al. [16] presented
LLM-Planner to generate behavior trees with commonsense
reasoning. Khandelwal et al. [17] introduced PromptIRL, using
language prompts for inferring reward functions from demon-
strations. These approaches highlight the potential of LLMs
to enhance RL-based robotic manipulation through improved
planning and interpretability.
III. PROPOSEDWORK
In this work, we present a hybrid framework that integrates
Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large Language Models
(LLMs) to achieve robust and adaptive robotic manipulation.
The proposed framework leverages the planning and reasoning
capabilities of LLMs for high-level task understanding and
decomposition, while RL ensures precise low-level task exe-
cution.
A. Framework Overview
The framework consists of three primary components:
•Task Planner (LLM-based): The Task Planner interprets
natural language instructions and decomposes them into
a sequence of subtasks.
•Skill Executor (RL-based): This component executes
each subtask in the simulation environment, relying on
trained RL policies for effective manipulation.
•Simulation Environment: The PyBullet simulation en-
vironment provides a realistic testing platform for evalu-
ating the hybrid framework. It includes the Franka Emika
Panda robotic arm, simulated sensory inputs, and various
objects for manipulation.
Fig. 1: System Architecture: Integration of LLM and RL for
Robotic Manipulation
B. Workflow Description
The overall workflow is as follows:
1)System Initialization: The system initializes the LLM,
RL agent, and simulation environment.
2)Natural Language Input: The user provides high-level
instructions, which are processed by the LLM.
3)Task Decomposition and Execution: The LLM decom-
poses the instruction into subtasks, which are sequen-
tially executed by the RL agent.
4)Feedback and Adaptation: The LLM continuously
monitors the environment for changes and updates the
task plan when necessary.
C. Simulation Environment
The PyBullet-based simulation environment is designed to
evaluate the proposed framework in various object manipu-
lation tasks, such as pick-and-place and obstacle avoidance.
The environment includes the Franka Emika Panda robot and
objects with varying properties.
Fig. 2: Simulation Environment: Franka Emika Panda Robot
in PyBullet

D. Integration of LLM and RL
The Task Planner (LLM) and Skill Executor (RL) commu-
nicate through an integration layer. The LLM module provides
high-level task decomposition, while the RL module ensures
precise execution of each subtask. A feedback loop between
the two modules enables dynamic task adaptation and error
recovery.
IV. METHODOLOGY
A. Simulation Environment
The proposed framework is developed and tested in a simu-
lation environment usingPyBullet, a physics-based simulation
platform. The simulation setup includes theFranka Emika
Pandarobotic arm, which is widely used for manipulation
tasks due to its high precision and flexibility. The environment
is designed to include various object manipulation scenarios
such as pick-and-place tasks, object sorting, and dynamic
obstacle avoidance. These tasks serve as benchmarks for
evaluating the performance of the proposed framework.
The task setup consists of:
•Aworkspacewith predefined positions for objects and
target locations.
•Sensory inputssimulated using depth cameras and force
sensors.
•Control strategiesimplemented using reinforcement
learning (RL) policies for executing low-level move-
ments.
This simulation setup provides a controlled environment for
training and testing the integration of reinforcement learning
and large language models.
B. Hybrid Framework
The hybrid framework integratesReinforcement Learning
(RL)for low-level task execution andLarge Language Mod-
els (LLMs)for high-level task planning. The overall structure
of this framework is depicted in Figure 3, illustrating the
interaction between these components.
Fig. 3: Hybrid Framework Integrating RL and LLMs1) Reinforcement Learning Module:The reinforcement
learning module is responsible for executing the low-level
control policies required for robot task execution. In this work,
we useProximal Policy Optimization (PPO)andSoft Actor-
Critic (SAC), two widely used RL algorithms, to train policies
for robot manipulation tasks.
The RL module operates as follows:
•State representation:The robot perceives the environ-
ment through sensory inputs, including joint positions,
velocities, and object positions.
•Action selection:Based on the learned policy, the RL
agent selects the optimal action to manipulate objects.
•Reward function:A custom reward function is designed
to encourage efficient and accurate task execution.
•Training process:The agent undergoes episodic training,
continuously refining its policy based on interaction with
the environment.
This module ensures that the robot can autonomously perform
physical interactions necessary for completing the assigned
tasks.
2) Large Language Model Module:The Large Language
Model (LLM) module is responsible for understanding and
interpreting high-level task instructions. We leverage models
such asGPT-based architecturesto process human-like com-
mands and translate them into structured subtask sequences.
Key functionalities:
•Task interpretation:LLMs parse human instructions
(e.g., ”Pick up the red cube and place it on the blue
platform”).
•Task decomposition:The high-level instruction is broken
down into smaller subtasks, such as ”Move to the cube,”
”Grasp the cube,” and ”Move to the target location.”
•Output generation:The LLM generates structured com-
mand sequences, which are then fed into the RL module
for execution.
This integration enables robots to follow complex, natural
language-based instructions, making them more adaptable to
human commands.
3) Integration:The integration of the RL and LLM mod-
ules is facilitated through anIntegration Layer, which serves
as the communication bridge between high-level planning and
low-level execution.
Pseudocode: LLM and RL Integration for Robotic Manipula-
tion
This integration allows the system to operate in a dynamic
manner, where the LLM provides reasoning and planning
capabilities, while RL ensures precise execution.
V. RESULTS ANDDISCUSSION
This section presents the results of the proposed hybrid
framework integrating Reinforcement Learning (RL) with
Large Language Models (LLMs) for robotic manipulation.
The evaluation was conducted in a PyBullet simulation en-
vironment using the Franka Emika Panda robot. The results

highlight improvements in task completion time, accuracy, and
adaptability compared to an RL-only approach.
A. Task Completion Time
Figure 4 illustrates the comparison of task completion time
between the RL-only and LLM+RL systems. The RL-only
system took an average of 18.5 seconds to complete tasks,
while the LLM+RL system reduced this time to 12.3 seconds,
representing a 33.5% improvement in efficiency.
Fig. 4: Task Completion Time Comparison
B. Accuracy and Adaptability
The proposed hybrid system also demonstrates significant
improvements in accuracy and adaptability, as shown in Fig-
ure 5. The LLM+RL system achieved an accuracy of 92.6%compared to 78.4% for the RL-only system. Similarly, the
adaptability increased from 65.2% in the RL-only system to
88.9% in the LLM+RL system, highlighting the robustness of
the proposed approach in dynamic environments.
Fig. 5: Accuracy and Adaptability Comparison
C. Task Completion Time Across Experiments
Figure 6 shows task completion time across 10 different
experimental runs. The RL-only system exhibited higher com-
pletion times with fluctuations, ranging from 17.5 to 19 sec-
onds. In contrast, the LLM+RL system maintained a consistent
average of approximately 12 seconds, demonstrating better
stability and efficiency.
Fig. 6: Task Completion Time Across Experiments
D. Learning Progress
The learning progress over 100 episodes is depicted in
Figure 7. The cumulative reward for the LLM+RL system
grew steadily and outperformed the RL-only system, reflect-

ing the enhanced learning capability provided by the hybrid
framework.
Fig. 7: Learning Progress Over Episodes
E. Performance Comparison
Table I summarizes the performance metrics for the RL-only
and LLM+RL systems. The LLM+RL system demonstrates
notable improvements in task completion time, accuracy, and
adaptability, reinforcing the effectiveness of integrating high-
level task planning from LLMs with low-level execution from
RL.

The results clearly demonstrate that integrating LLMs into
robotic manipulation tasks significantly improves performance
across multiple metrics. The hybrid framework’s ability to
interpret high-level natural language instructions and adapt to
dynamic environments makes it more robust and efficient than
traditional RL-based approaches. The feedback mechanism
between the LLM and RL components ensures continuous task
refinement, resulting in improved accuracy and adaptability.
These findings highlight the potential for broader applications
of LLM+RL systems in real-world robotic scenarios.
VI. CONCLUSION
This paper presents a hybrid framework that combines
Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Large Language Models
(LLMs) to enhance robotic manipulation tasks. Results from
PyBullet simulations using the Franka Emika Panda robot indi-
cate notable improvements in task completion time, accuracy,
and adaptability when compared to systems relying solely onRL. The LLM+RL approach achieves a 33.5 % reduction
in task completion time, while also boosting accuracy and
adaptability by 18.1% and 36.4%, respectively. This integra-
tion allows for dynamic task adaptation and the ability to
process natural language instructions, thereby making robotic
systems more efficient and resilient. Future research will aim
at real-world implementation, scalability for multiple robots,
and improving sim-to-real transfer to broaden the framework’s
applicability.

structure.title: INTRODUCTION
structure.summary: This partial document introduces a novel hybrid framework for robotic manipulation that integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large Language Models (LLMs). The core idea is to leverage RL for precise low-level control of robotic actions and LLMs for high-level task planning, natural language understanding, and reasoning. This combination aims to enable robots to interpret and execute complex, human-like instructions, adapt to dynamic environments, and improve overall efficiency, accuracy, and adaptability in manipulation tasks. The framework is evaluated in a PyBullet simulation using a Franka Emika Panda robotic arm, demonstrating significant improvements in task completion time, accuracy, and adaptability compared to RL-only systems. The document also briefly touches upon related work in the field, highlighting previous research in RL for manipulation and the emerging trend of integrating LLMs into robotic systems. Future research directions include sim-to-real transfer, scalability, and multi-robot systems.

structure.title: RELATEDWORK
structure.summary:
This partial document introduces a hybrid framework for robotic manipulation that integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large Language Models (LLMs). The main points covered are:

*   **Problem:** Existing robotic systems, while advanced in AI and ML, have a gap in merging RL for low-level control with LLMs for high-level reasoning and natural language understanding.
*   **Proposed Solution:** A hybrid framework that uses LLMs for high-level task planning and decomposition of natural language instructions, and RL for precise low-level execution of these subtasks.
*   **Framework Components:**
    *   **Task Planner (LLM-based):** Interprets natural language and breaks down tasks into subtasks.
    *   **Skill Executor (RL-based):** Executes the subtasks using trained RL policies.
    *   **Simulation Environment:** A PyBullet-based environment with a Franka Emika Panda robotic arm for testing.
*   **Workflow:** The system initializes, receives natural language input, the LLM decomposes it into subtasks for the RL agent to execute, and the LLM provides feedback and adaptation to environmental changes.
*   **Evaluation:** The framework is tested in simulation with the Franka Emika Panda robot on various manipulation scenarios.
*   **Results:** The hybrid framework shows significant improvements in task completion time, accuracy, and adaptability compared to RL-only systems.
*   **Future Work:** Exploration of sim-to-real transfer, scalability, and multi-robot systems.
*   **Related Work:** A review of existing research on integrating RL and LLMs in robotics, including specific frameworks and approaches for task planning, control, and natural language interaction.

structure.title: PROPOSEDWORK
structure.summary: This partial document discusses the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for robotic manipulation. It highlights recent research trends in robotics that combine high-level semantic reasoning with low-level control, emphasizing how LLMs can bridge the gap in RL's ability to interpret complex instructions. Several existing approaches are mentioned, including LLMs for trajectory generation, a framework linking LLMs with ROS for accessible robot programming, dynamic reward specification, internal task reasoning, grounding LLM plans, generating behavior trees with commonsense reasoning, and inferring reward functions from demonstrations. The document then proposes a hybrid framework that integrates LLMs and RL for robust and adaptive robotic manipulation. This framework consists of an LLM-based Task Planner for interpreting natural language and decomposing tasks, an RL-based Skill Executor for precise low-level task execution, and a PyBullet simulation environment for evaluation. The workflow involves system initialization, natural language input, task decomposition and execution by the RL agent, and continuous feedback and adaptation by the LLM. The simulation environment is described as a PyBullet-based platform featuring a Franka Emika Panda robotic arm and various objects for manipulation tasks.

nodes.title: Integration of LLM and RL
nodes.summary:
This partial document describes a hybrid framework that integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for robust and adaptive robotic manipulation. The framework leverages LLMs for high-level task understanding and decomposition through natural language instructions, and RL for precise low-level task execution.

The document outlines the following key components and workflows:

*   **Framework Overview:**
    *   **Task Planner (LLM-based):** Interprets natural language instructions and breaks them into subtasks.
    *   **Skill Executor (RL-based):** Executes subtasks using trained RL policies.
    *   **Simulation Environment:** A PyBullet environment with a Franka Emika Panda robotic arm for testing.
*   **Workflow Description:**
    1.  System initialization.
    2.  User provides natural language instructions.
    3.  LLM decomposes instructions into subtasks for RL execution.
    4.  LLM monitors the environment and adapts the task plan as needed.
*   **Simulation Environment Details:**
    *   Uses PyBullet with a Franka Emika Panda robot.
    *   Includes various object manipulation scenarios (pick-and-place, obstacle avoidance).
    *   Simulated sensory inputs (depth cameras, force sensors).
*   **Integration of LLM and RL:**
    *   An integration layer facilitates communication between the LLM (planning) and RL (execution).
    *   A feedback loop enables dynamic adaptation and error recovery.
*   **Methodology:**
    *   **Reinforcement Learning Module:** Uses PPO and SAC algorithms for low-level control, with state representation, action selection, and reward functions.
    *   **Large Language Model Module:** Leverages GPT-based architectures for task interpretation, decomposition into subtasks, and structured command generation.
    *   **Integration:** An integration layer connects the LLM and RL modules for dynamic operation.

The document also references previous research on LLMs in robotics, including their application in agricultural picking, general reviews of LLMs in robotics, zero-shot trajectory generation, and frameworks like ROS-LLM. It highlights recent advances in combining high-level reasoning with low-level control, and specific approaches like dynamic reward specification, internal task reasoning, grounding LLM plans, behavior tree generation, and inferring reward functions from demonstrations.

structure.title: METHODOLOGY
structure.summary: The partial document describes a hybrid framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) for high-level task planning and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for low-level robotic execution. The LLM module interprets natural language instructions, decomposes them into subtasks, and generates structured commands. The RL module, using algorithms like PPO and SAC, learns policies to execute these subtasks through physical interaction with the environment. An integration layer facilitates communication between the LLM and RL modules, enabling dynamic task adaptation and error recovery. The framework is developed and tested in a PyBullet simulation environment using a Franka Emika Panda robotic arm, with scenarios including pick-and-place, object sorting, and obstacle avoidance. The simulation setup includes a workspace, simulated sensory inputs (depth cameras, force sensors), and RL-based control strategies. The results section will present the evaluation of this framework.

structure.title: RESULTS ANDDISCUSSION
structure.summary:
This partial document describes a hybrid framework for robotic manipulation that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) for high-level task planning and Reinforcement Learning (RL) for low-level execution. The framework is developed and tested in a PyBullet simulation environment using a Franka Emika Panda robotic arm.

Key points covered include:

*   **Integration of LLM and RL:** The LLM acts as a Task Planner, decomposing high-level instructions into subtasks, while the RL module serves as a Skill Executor, precisely carrying out these subtasks. A feedback loop allows for dynamic task adaptation and error recovery.
*   **Simulation Environment:** The use of PyBullet for physics-based simulation, featuring the Franka Emika Panda robot, and scenarios like pick-and-place, object sorting, and obstacle avoidance. The environment includes a workspace, simulated sensory inputs (depth cameras, force sensors), and RL-based control strategies.
*   **Hybrid Framework Components:**
    *   **Reinforcement Learning Module:** Responsible for low-level control policies, using algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). It involves state representation, action selection, a custom reward function, and episodic training.
    *   **Large Language Model Module:** Interprets high-level task instructions (e.g., from human commands), decomposes them into subtasks, and generates structured command sequences for the RL module. GPT-based architectures are mentioned.
    *   **Integration Layer:** Acts as a communication bridge between the LLM and RL modules.
*   **Results and Discussion:** The document presents comparative results showing improvements of the LLM+RL system over an RL-only approach in terms of:
    *   **Task Completion Time:** A significant reduction in time (33.5% improvement).
    *   **Accuracy and Adaptability:** Higher accuracy (92.6% vs. 78.4%) and increased adaptability (88.9% vs. 65.2%).
    *   **Stability:** More consistent task completion times across multiple experimental runs.
    *   **Learning Progress:** Higher cumulative rewards achieved by the LLM+RL system.

nodes.title: Task Completion Time
nodes.summary:
This partial document describes an algorithm for integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for robotic manipulation. The algorithm involves initializing both LLM and RL agents, parsing natural language instructions into subtasks using the LLM, and then querying the RL agent to execute these subtasks. The environment state is monitored, and the task plan is updated by the LLM if changes occur. The document then presents experimental results comparing this LLM+RL approach to an RL-only approach, highlighting improvements in:

*   **Task Completion Time:** The LLM+RL system achieved a 33.5% improvement, reducing average completion time from 18.5 seconds to 12.3 seconds.
*   **Accuracy:** The LLM+RL system achieved 92.6% accuracy compared to 78.4% for the RL-only system.
*   **Adaptability:** The LLM+RL system showed increased adaptability from 65.2% to 88.9%.
*   **Consistency:** The LLM+RL system demonstrated more stable and consistent task completion times across multiple experiments.
*   **Learning Progress:** The LLM+RL system showed a steadily growing cumulative reward over episodes, outperforming the RL-only system.

nodes.title: Learning Progress
nodes.summary:
This partial document describes a hybrid framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for robotic manipulation. The core idea is to leverage LLMs for high-level task planning and natural language understanding, and RL for low-level execution and control.

The document outlines an algorithm (Algorithm 1) that initializes both LLM and RL agents, sets up a simulation environment, and then iteratively parses natural language instructions into subtasks using the LLM. The RL agent is then queried to execute these subtasks, while the environment state is monitored. If the environment changes, the LLM updates the task plan.

The document then presents experimental results comparing this LLM+RL approach to an RL-only approach, highlighting significant improvements in:

*   **Task Completion Time:** The LLM+RL system reduced completion time by 33.5% (from 18.5s to 12.3s on average).
*   **Accuracy:** The LLM+RL system achieved 92.6% accuracy compared to 78.4% for RL-only.
*   **Adaptability:** Adaptability increased from 65.2% to 88.9% with the LLM+RL system.
*   **Stability:** The LLM+RL system demonstrated more consistent task completion times across experiments.
*   **Learning Progress:** The LLM+RL system showed a better cumulative reward over episodes.

The document concludes that integrating LLMs with RL for robotic manipulation leads to more efficient, accurate, and adaptable systems, capable of processing natural language and adapting to dynamic environments. Future work is planned for real-world implementation and scalability.
